title: SUM, AVERAGE, and AVERAGEA apply Excel's 50-exponent cancellation snap once at the final numeric addition
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527 (dc-ss3b), SUM snaps its final result to +0 when the last left partial sum's binary exponent exceeds the sum's binary exponent by at least 50 (so SUM(0.1,0.2,-0.3) returns +0 rather than 2^-54). A trailing numeric 0 counts as the final addition and suppresses the snap (SUM(0.1,0.2,-0.3,0) returns 2^-54, 0x3c90000000000000), whereas trailing cell text, logicals, and blanks are skipped and do not suppress it. AVERAGE and AVERAGEA apply the same rule to their numerator before dividing by the count; SUMPRODUCT does not snap.
basis: Measured across 98+ Excel 16.0.20527 probes in dc-ss3b (docs/research/sum-cancellation-2026-11-12.md) covering scales 2^-900 to 2^900, exponent gaps 49 vs 50, zero vs skipped tails, and AVERAGE/AVERAGEA/SUMPRODUCT controls; full-bank SUM (1,211/1,211), AVERAGE (1,222/1,222), and AVERAGEA (1,212/1,212) remain matched.
inferred: That the shared post-addition snap uses the exact 50-exponent threshold across every binade is inferred from the dc-ss3b power-of-two boundary sweeps; the raw probe JSON files were archived to R2 (research/round53/20261112-fn2-0327/) rather than committed to git.
